rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Norovirus spreads easily in hospitals, care homes, schools, nurseries and other close-contact settings.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Handwashing with soap and warm water is important because alcohol hand sanitiser does not reliably kill norovirus.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: People should remain away from work or school until 48 hours after vomiting and diarrhoea have stopped.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Food preparation for others should be avoided until 48 hours after symptoms end.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Contaminated clothing, bedding, toilets, taps and door handles require thorough cleaning or disinfection.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Health and social-care settings should use structured outbreak recognition, isolation and communication procedures.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Vomiting and diarrhoea clusters in residential settings require coordinated infection-prevention action.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Replacing lost fluids helps reduce dehydration risk during illness.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Norovirus risk depends on setting, crowding, surface contamination, hygiene, symptom timing and vulnerable occupants.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Norovirus evidence is outbreak-, setting-, contact-, hygiene- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: The Environment Agency monitors E. coli and intestinal enterococci at designated bathing waters.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Monitoring also looks for indicators such as cyanobacteria, macro-algae, marine phytoplankton and waste.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Designated bathing waters are classified annually as excellent, good, sufficient or poor.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Local councils must display advice against bathing when a site is classified as poor.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Signs for poor bathing waters must explain pollution causes and actions being taken.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Short-term pollution warnings are intended to inform bathers about temporary health risks.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: The bathing-water season in England runs from 15 May to 30 September for designation criteria.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Current bathing-water information can be displayed using Environment Agency data widgets.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Bathing-water risk depends on microbial results, recent pollution, weather, catchment conditions, signage and exposure.

rows.source: Environment Agency bathing-water safety
rows.verified: Bathing-water evidence is site-, sample-, season-, pollution-event- and user-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
